title: Queen's Gambit Declined: Exchange Variation
line: White trades pawns in the center, then pushes two queenside pawns against three.

steps.text: Black guards its center pawn with the king pawn and brings a knight out.
Trade pawns on d5. The center is set now, and you can make a plan around it.

also.c1g5: That pins the knight, the main line. This lesson trades on d5 first.
also.g1f3: That is sound too. This lesson trades on d5 first.

steps.after: Now White has two pawns on the queenside against Black's three. That count matters later.

steps.text: Bring the bishop out and pin the knight to the queen.
steps.after: Black adds a pawn to guard the center.

steps.text: Move the pawn in front of your king one square to free your other bishop.
Both sides bring out their pieces and castle. Black's pawns stand on c6 and d5.
Put a rook behind the pawn on b2. It is there to push the pawn forward.
Push the pawn on b2 two squares. It heads for b5 to strike at the pawn on c6.
steps.after: Black stops the pawn for now.

steps.text: Push the pawn on a2 two squares. It backs up the push of your other pawn to b5.
Now push the pawn to b5. If pawns trade there, Black is left with a weak pawn on c6 or d5.
steps.after: This plan is called the minority attack: fewer pawns attack more to leave a weak one behind.

summary: White trades in the center, then pushes two queenside pawns against three to leave Black a weak pawn.
